Back when the whole Somali pirate thing was going on, I seriously considered going into privateering -- to the extent that I actually started calculating the costs of such an operation. They're surprisingly low.

To start, you'll need a sailboat, like this one, for example, or perhaps this one (which is almost too good a deal to be true; I wonder what's wrong with her). Anything less than 30' will not do. Ideally you'd want something in the 40-45' range, but those get pricey real quick. If you know what you're doing, you can probably find one for dirt cheap that just needs a little TLC. I'd budget about $20K for the boat and getting her ready to rumble.

A 30-35' boat can technically be sailed single-handed, but that's dangerous and lonely. I would recommend a crew of four. That's enough to handle the vessel without sacrificing too much comfort.

The biggest problem is arming the vessel. In most countries, you'll be arrested if you try to clear customs with firearms on board. Best case scenario, you get to check your guns with the local constabulary; and good luck getting them back when you want to ship out!

There are three solutions to this problem:

  1. Cache your weapons in a remote area before trying to clear in with no weapons on board. Given that it's super illegal to let your feet touch land before you clear in, this is not a very good solution unless you really know what you're doing and have a deep familiarity with the place you're going.
  2. Work with another boat. Load all the weapons onto Boat #2 which stays outside the 12-mile limit. Only Boat #1 clears in. Switch off next time you need to make port.
  3. Build concealed compartments in the boat. This is dodgy, because if (gods forbid) you're boarded, the coasties will wise to your scheme very quickly. You are not savvy enough to outsmart the coasties. They have busted many drug smugglers and know where to look.

Once you've figured out how you're going to deal with the "cargo manifest contains various delightful implements of death" problem, time to load up! Obviously the choice of armament will depend on personal taste, but if I were trying to do this, I'd take two .30-06 deer rifles, a sawed-off 12ga shotgun, two spear guns, and a bunch of homemade mortars. Total outlay, another $8-10K or so. Resist the temptation to get a Barrett. .30-06 rounds are more than enough to fuck up an outboard motor.

You will then provision the boat with enough food and drink to get you where you want to go. Cooking at sea is a fine art which is beyond the scope of this analysis; but you will want to bring fishing gear, because you're about to develop a deep appreciation for sashimi.

You will then go to the pirate-infested waters of your choice and pretend to be oblivious rich bastards.
